skill.name: model-per-chat
skill.description: Load when someone runs many Claude Code / Claude desktop chats, agents, subagents or scheduled tasks and wants to decide which model each one should use (Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, or no model at all) to save plan limits or money without adding mistakes. Use it when a new model comes out ("Fable 5.2 just came out, who gets it?"), when limits run out too fast, or for "which model for each chat", "assign models to my agents", "save tokens across sessions", "qué modelo le pongo a cada chat", "a quién le pongo Fable", "Opus o Sonnet", "ahorrar límites", "se me acaba el plan", "que suba el esfuerzo solo", "Opus también es caro", "lo mejor pagando poco". It sets a cheap base (mid model, low effort) with a written rule to climb to the top model only for the hard or irreversible step and come back down. It reads the live plan meters and each session's current model, checks today's prices and plan rules on the official pages, scores every chat 1-10 by what a mistake there costs, maps the score and the run frequency to a model, flags plan traps (models billed outside the limits, launch windows that end, extra usage switched off), and only downgrades a chat after a check on its real recent work. Not for choosing a model inside API code (use claude-api) and not for one single task.

content.user_title: Assign Models Across Chats and Scheduled Tasks
content.value_statement: Using one expensive model across every chat can exhaust limits, while careless downgrades can reduce quality. This skill guides model assignments using task importance, frequency, current plan rules, and quality checks.
actual_capabilities: Guide collection of current plan meters, session models, effort settings, and official pricing rules.
Inventory chats and scheduled jobs by purpose, frequency, affected systems, and reviewer.
Score mistake consequences and map workload importance to relative model cost.
Draft escalation rules for difficult steps, repeated failures, and irreversible actions.
Define downgrade comparisons and rollback criteria using recent representative tasks.
Report proposed assignments, confirmed changes, unsupported switches, and important plan dates.
limitations: Requires access to session metadata, usage meters, and current official sources; no integration code is included.
Does not measure exact subscription cost per turn or guarantee savings.
Cannot guarantee automatic model switching; scheduled-task defaults require verification on a subsequent run.
Targets multiple chats and jobs, not model selection inside API code or one isolated task.

use_cases.title: Balance Development Sessions
use_cases.description: Separate routine coding work from complex debugging and release decisions, with stronger-model review where errors matter most.
use_cases.target_user: Developers managing several Claude Code sessions

use_cases.title: Reduce Scheduled Monitoring Costs
use_cases.description: Identify frequent jobs that can use smaller models or scripts, then verify the actual model used on their next run.

use_cases.title: Protect Client Work Quality
use_cases.description: Keep approval work on stronger models while assigning routine preparation to cheaper models with clear escalation and rollback rules.

prompt_templates.title: Inventory My Chats
prompt_templates.prompt: Help inventory my chats and scheduled jobs. Ask for each purpose, current model, effort, run frequency, affected systems, and reviewer.

prompt_templates.title: Recommend Model Assignments
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my chat inventory and current plan meters. Check official plan rules, score mistake consequences, and recommend models without changing settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare workload importance with plan limits

prompt_templates.title: Write Escalation Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft per-chat escalation rules for hard steps, repeated failures, and irreversible actions. Preserve owner approval requirements and mark unsupported delegation features.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Batch Downgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a batch downgrade with isolated replay checks, rollback criteria, and scheduled-run verification. Request approval before settings changes or live actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: validate changes before applying them

output_examples.input: My monitoring job runs every 20 minutes, while a supervisor approves customer messages. Where should I reduce costs?
output: Monitoring: evaluate a small model or script for routine checks, then verify quality and the next scheduled run.
Supervisor: retain a stronger base model because mistakes affect customers.
Status: recommendations only; no settings changes or measured savings reported.

output_examples.input: Prepare a cheaper setup for coding chats without weakening release checks.
output: Routine coding: consider a midrange base model with lower effort after representative checks pass.
Hard debugging: delegate the difficult step after two failed attempts, then return to the base model.
Release actions: require stronger-model review and existing owner approvals.
Rollback: restore the stronger model if the reviewer returns two pieces of work within one week.

best_practices: Collect current usage meters and official plan rules before recommending assignments.
Use isolated, read-only replay checks; obtain explicit approval before settings changes or repeated live actions.
Verify actual session models after changes and document clear rollback criteria.
anti_patterns: Downgrading every chat solely because a smaller model is cheaper.
Replaying customer messages, spending, deployments, or deletion against live systems as a quality test.
Claiming savings or completed switches without measurements or session verification.

faq.question: Does this skill switch every chat automatically?
faq.answer: No. Changes depend on available tools and owner approval. The workflow requires reading session models back to confirm successful switches.

faq.question: Can it calculate exact subscription costs per turn?
faq.answer: No. It compares relative costs and observed meter movement because exact subscription multipliers may not be published.

faq.question: How does it choose a model?
faq.answer: It scores mistake consequences, considers run frequency and review coverage, and checks current official plan rules.

faq.question: Does a scheduled task have its own model setting?
faq.answer: Not always. Some tasks inherit application defaults. The actual model must be verified on the next scheduled run.

faq.question: How should I test a cheaper model?
faq.answer: Compare representative recent tasks using isolated fixtures or dry runs. Do not repeat live actions without explicit approval.

faq.question: Is this an API model router for Claude or Codex?
faq.answer: No. It provides a planning workflow for multiple chats and jobs, not API routing code or guaranteed integrations.
